title: Putin’s bot army is targeting German and French elections, Sweden warns
content:
STOCKHOLM — Russia poses a threat to upcoming elections in Europe’s biggest democracies and social media platforms must “step up” the fight against Moscow’s networks of bots, Sweden’s disinformation defense chief has warned. 

In an interview with POLITICO, Magnus Hjort, director general of the Swedish Psychological Defence Agency, said elections were an “opportunity” for Vladimir Putin’s information war machine to try to polarize and divide European societies.

The Kremlin’s key objective is to make voters doubt whether their politicians should keep sending money and weapons to Kyiv by peddling fake stories about Ukrainian corruption and other abuses, he added.

Hjort and his team do not believe Moscow is targeting Sunday’s general election in Sweden — in part because the country is largely united behind the policy of supporting Ukraine.

Instead, he said, Russia is aiming at more powerful countries with elections on the horizon — including German state votes and the French presidential campaign — where far-right parties seen as more sympathetic to Moscow are poised to make gains.

title: January 2026 Protests: Report on the Latest Status of Aref Assar in Torbat-e Heydarieh Prison

According to information received by HRANA, on August 8, 2026, Mr. Assar reported to Torbat-e Heydarieh Prison to begin serving his two-year-and-six-month prison sentence.

At the initial stage, he was sentenced by the Khaf Revolutionary Court to five years and one day of imprisonment. After the case was referred to the Court of Appeals, the sentence was reduced to two years and six months of imprisonment. During the proceedings, he faced multiple charges, including “propaganda against the regime,” “cooperation with hostile countries,” “espionage,” “disrupting public security,” “insulting the Supreme Leader,” and “links with opposition groups.”

An informed source close to his family told HRANA that no specific evidence against Mr. Assar was presented in his case and that a significant portion of the allegations against him was based on statements made by individuals who had reported him. The source added: “Mr. Assar was subjected to mistreatment and torture while in detention, which resulted in a dislocated shoulder. The injury has so far required him to undergo several surgeries on his shoulder.”

title: Australia: 25 Years of Abusive Offshore Detention
content:
(Sydney) – The Australian government has caused thousands of people seeking asylum to suffer grave abuses under its offshore detention system, which began in September 2001, Human Rights Watch said today.

Over the past 25 years, Australia has forcibly transferred more than 5,000 asylum seekers to Naoero (formerly called Nauru) and Manus Island, Papua New Guinea (PNG). Those transferred have experienced inhumane conditions and serious harm to their mental and physical health. The United Nations refugee agency, other countries, and human rights groups including Human Rights Watch, have repeatedly pressed Australia to end offshore processing. 

“Australia’s offshore detention policy has caused profound harm to men, women, and children seeking refuge since its introduction 25 years ago,” said Annabel Hennessy, Australia researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Rather than abiding by its international legal obligations toward asylum seekers, Australia has hardened its abusive policies, contributing to a global erosion of refugee law.”

title: The Rising Baseball Star, a Fatal Car Crash and the Fixer
content:
Around 4 a.m. on Sept. 21, 2020, Luis David Saba arrived at a desolate stretch of highway along the southern coast of the Dominican Republic. Police and paramedics had left by then, taking with them a Jeep Grand Cherokee with a crumpled hood and the tangled remains of the cheap motorcycle it had smashed into. Also gone were the motorcycle’s two critically injured passengers. The only signs that an accident had occurred a few hours earlier were the blood and debris smeared across the asphalt and a pile of neatly placed branches.

Saba knew what to expect underneath that pile. It was a Dominican custom to use anything on hand to shroud a body abandoned by paramedics. Pushing away the branches, Saba saw shredded clothes, torn skin and long, curly hair forming a halo over a battered face. He covered the body of his 20-year-old younger brother, Yohan Saba Mercado, with a sheet. In shock, he felt nothing but the need to get his brother out of the road.

title: 9/11 transformed our relationship with news – and laid the groundwork for today’s crisis of trust
content:
Twenty-five years on, the legacy of the September 11 attacks continues beyond the initial physical and economic effects. The events of 9/11 and the subsequent “war on terror” severely undermined trust in mainstream news media in the US and around the world, laying the groundwork for today’s fractured, hyperpartisan information environment.

In the days and weeks after the attacks, American journalists faced a dilemma: maintain professional standards of objectivity, balance and impartiality or “rally round the flag” in support of the state. Many chose the latter, and a powerful mood of patriotic sentiment echoed around US newsrooms. Journalists and news anchors wore stars-and-stripe pin badges, while networks adopted slogans such as “America Under Attack” for evening news bulletins.

Veteran news anchor Dan Rather captured this patriotic tone during an emotional interview with late-night host David Letterman: “George Bush is the president, he makes the decisions … wherever he wants me to line up, just tell me where”.

In an address days after the attacks, Bush set the narrative that would define much of the post-9/11 era:

title: WACANA Puts Self-determination at The Center of AI Literacy
content:
Published to mark International Literacy Day, 8 September 2026

This year marks the 60th International Literacy Day, under the theme “Literacy for people, the planet, and prosperity.” Sixty years on, literacy means more than reading and writing. It also means being able to question the information in front of us, understand the technologies shaping it, and decide on our own terms what role those technologies should play in our lives.

As Hardiansyah, Chair of the Executive Board of Wikimedia Indonesia, puts it:

“Literacy is not only about reading or writing; it is also about opening a window to the world. Through Wikimedia’s open knowledge movement, we can make knowledge freely available in Indonesian and in many other languages so that anyone can access it. This spirit of openness means that knowledge is not something held by only a few but a shared resource that everyone can benefit from.”

title: Marvel’s Wolverine review – a gloriously conflicted lead is let down by crude, boring battling
content:
PlayStation 5; Insomniac Games
Logan is well realised by Liam McIntyre and some exquisite character art, but there are lapses in narrative and emotional arcs and some of the combat feels like a chore

It was always going to be difficult to follow Spider-Man. Insomniac’s three games based around the web-slinger are masterpieces of superhero wish fulfilment, allowing you to swoop above a depiction of Manhattan alive with graffiti artists, roving journalists and gun-toting gangsters. If anyone should be up to the task, it’s Wolverine. A beloved Marvel stalwart, his life much darker and bloodier than Peter Parker’s, he seems the ideal protagonist for a moody action adventure. Yet somehow this well-made game falls short of its potential.

title: Uusi selvitys: Sosiaalinen media johdattaa tehokkaasti pidempien tekstien äärelle

Milloin viimeksi istuit rauhassa lukemassa kirjaa tunnin ajan? Lukemiset tavat ovat muuttuneet perusteellisesti, osoittaa SLS:n äskettäin julkaistu lukemista ja kirjallisuutta koskeva selvitys. Kirjallisuusalan on sopeuduttava uuteen todellisuuteen, jos haluamme, että suomalaiset lukevat jatkossakin pitkiä tekstejä.

Laadullisessa selvityksessä haastateltiin 36 suomalaista, jotka lukevat pidempiä tekstejä useita kertoja viikossa tai ainakin kerran kuukaudessa. Heitä pyydettiin kuvailemaan, milloin, missä ja miten he kuluttavat pidempiä sisältöjä, kuten kirjoja, lehtiartikkeleita, äänikirjoja tai podcasteja.

title: Von der Leyen backs space mega-deal despite looming EU antitrust probe
content:
PARIS — European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has publicly endorsed a proposed space venture between Airbus, Leonardo and Thales — a rare intervention by a top EU official in an ongoing competition matter — as the satellite-makers seek Brussels’ approval for the deal.

EU officials generally refrain from commenting on open antitrust proceedings. The Commission received a rap on the knuckles in 2015 from the European Ombudsman after former competition chief Joaquín Almunia made public comments on an ongoing investigation into a banking cartel. 

Von der Leyen’s high-profile backing comes as the three satellite-makers hold informal talks with the Commission’s competition directorate on the €6.5 billion deal, which raises complex antitrust issues and could require divestments to win approval. They have yet to submit a formal notification for a merger review.

She is also a prime mover behind an overhaul of the EU’s merger guidelines, which in addition to traditional competition concerns would allow greater latitude for mergers that create so-called European champions.

title: The Dominican Baseball Factory
content:
On an evening in late 2021, in a pristine baseball complex in central Santo Domingo, a baby-faced 14-year-old outfielder in athletic gear named Belfi Rivera huddled in front of a computer screen. Next to him was John Carmona, who had been Belfi’s trainer and de facto caretaker since he was 11 years old. In a nearby office, Belfi’s parents stared anxiously at a separate computer. On the screen, calling into the Dominican Republic, were representatives of the Arizona Diamondbacks, there for a conversation that promised to shift forever the fortunes of Belfi and his parents.

The team, they would soon learn, had agreed to pay Belfi $1.8 million after his 16th birthday. It was a deal Carmona had negotiated without consulting Belfi or his parents. It was also a handshake agreement that skirted Major League Baseball’s rules that bar teams from signing players younger than 16. Every year, all 30 major league teams reach preacuerdos, or early deals, with hundreds of Dominican prospects — a practice they make little attempt to hide. (The Diamondbacks did not respond to a request for comment.)

title: The rebuilding in Nepal needs to start now. This is what worked after an earthquake a decade ago – and what to avoid
content:
In the aftermath of the devastating flash floods in Nepal on August 26, the immediate priority was to save lives and meet the urgent needs of victims. But the relief efforts must also begin laying the foundations for the future.

This requires a delicate balancing act. The early days after a disaster are crucial for ensuring a long-term recovery sets off in the right direction.

This means addressing challenging questions about how and where to rebuild homes, even while rescue efforts are ongoing and debris is being cleared. It also means ensuring aid agencies and policymakers are investing humanitarian funding in the right way and listening to communities.

After a 7.8-magnitude earthquake struck Nepal in 2015, killing nearly 9,000 people, I led a review of the recovery efforts of 15 of the largest international NGOs and their partners, which had received around US$100 million of funding from the United Kingdom’s Disasters Emergency Committee (DEC) and the Canadian Humanitarian Coalition.

While that earthquake was very different to the recent flood catastrophe in terms of scale, spread and severity, there are still many lessons about what to do after a disaster – and what not to do.

title: A Slovene in Armenia: The Best Wiki Experience of My Life
content:
In August 2026, as part of CEE Hub‘s Peer Learning Exchange, I travelled from Slovenia to Armenia to take part in the Summer WikiCamp, organised by Wikimedia Armenia and held in Tsaghkadzor. In my head, the plan behind the exchange was pretty straightforward: I would participate in WikiCamp activities, learn from the organisers, connect with people, spend some time there, and that’s it. But pretty quickly I realised it was going to be a completely different experience from what I had anticipated.

Let me start by saying that I have been to quite a few Wikimedia events by now. I have attended conferences, meetings, edit-a-thons, workshops, and Wikimania. I have met hundreds of people, worked on projects, given presentations, and spent countless hours talking about Wikipedia.

And yet… somehow, a WikiCamp in Armenia became the best Wikimedia experience of my life.

title: Apple unveils folding iPhone Duo as new CEO takes center stage
content:

title: When a little snout can LIFT the world
content:
Animal welfare is now well integrated in people’s minds and aims to make sure that animals are healthy, comfortable, well-fed, safe and able to express natural behaviors without unnecessary pain, fear or distress.

Animal welfare has traditionally focused on preventing suffering, with research emphasising negative experiences. Today, growing scientific interest and public expectations are shifting attention toward positive welfare, ensuring animals can also experience positive states. However, researchers have yet to agree on how to define or measure positive welfare, meaning no current farm animal welfare assessment includes direct animal-based indicators of positive experiences.

The COST Action LIFT will advance this emerging field through multidisciplinary research, cross-disciplinary knowledge sharing, training, and collaboration across Europe, helping lay the foundations for future progress in positive animal welfare research. Industry, government, NGOs, veterinary organisations, and farm advisory bodies are involved throughout the project to ensure practical solutions that strengthen animal welfare and support a more sustainable livestock sector.

title: Växtbaserade alternativ till mjölk och kött är huvudsakligen säkra, men inte helt riskfria
content:
Växtbaserade alternativ till mjölk och kött erbjuder konsumenterna näringsmässiga och miljömässiga fördelar, men deras säkerhetsprofil skiljer sig från animaliska livsmedel. Enligt en översiktsartikel från Livsmedelsverket och VTT bör särskild uppmärksamhet fästas vid mögelgifter, vissa metaller samt sporbildande bakterier i dessa produkter.

Översiktsartikeln, som publicerats i tidskriften Food Science & Nutrition, sammanfattar forskningsresultat om kemiska och mikrobiologiska faror samt näringsmässiga egenskaper hos växtbaserade mjölk- och köttalternativ. Artikeln bygger på internationella studier, och mer detaljerad information om växtbaserade alternativ till mjölkprodukter på den finländska marknaden kommer att presenteras vid slutseminariet för projektet VEGETURVA den 17 september.

– Riskprofilen för växtbaserade produkter skiljer sig från den för mjölk och kött. De kan innehålla vissa kemiska faror som sällan förekommer i animaliska produkter, men samtidigt förekommer färre sjukdomsalstrande mikroorganismer som är förknippade med animaliska råvaror, säger forskningsprofessor Johanna Suomi vid Livsmedelsverket.

title: Grow Nordic & Baltic Programme Opens Applications For Startups Ready To Scale Across Borders. Apply by 25.9.
content:
A startup can have a strong product and a promising market at home. Taking the next step — entering a neighbouring country, building the right network or preparing for international investment — is a different challenge altogether.

The programme has been created to help startups make that transition. The cross-border programme brings together startup ecosystems in Finland, Sweden and Estonia, giving selected teams the opportunity to work with mentors, coaches and other founders across the region as they prepare for international growth.

GNB is co-funded by the European Union’s Interreg Central Baltic Programme and jointly organised by , , and .

The programme begins in November with a baseline analysis of each participating startup. The aim is straightforward: to understand where a team is now and what it needs to work on next.

Based on this assessment, each startup will receive a tailored coaching roadmap. Over the course of the programme, founders will work with mentors and experts on areas including their business model, growth strategy and preparations for entering new markets.

title: A New AI Ethics Framework for Zooniverse
content:
This post was written by Hillary Burgess and Sam Blickhan.

In June 2025, we announced an initiative to develop a set of recommendations for running AI/ML-engaged projects on the Zooniverse platform. After a year of collaboration and discussion with volunteers, experts in ethics, communications, AI, and participatory research, as well as Zooniverse project leads (noting that these groups are not mutually exclusive!), we are excited to finally share the results of this work.

Today, we launch the first-ever Zooniverse AI Ethics Framework, composed of Key Principles, internal actions taken by Zooniverse, and Recommendations for Project Teams that will guide the use of AI/ML on the platform going forward. This is a living Framework, and we are committed to improving and iterating as we receive feedback and the technological, social, and cultural context continue to evolve. This new page also includes information about AI/ML on Zooniverse, FAQs, and resources to learn more. You can find the new page at https://www.zooniverse.org/about/ai-ethics.

So, how did we get here?

title: Culture in National & Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs)
content:
This article is an extract of a special edition of the Brussels Decoder, Culture Action Europe’s monthly members-only publication containing regular updates and analysis on EU(ropean) cultural policy and politics. If you wish to receive regular updates on the MFF and other EU(ropean) cultural policy developments in the future, consider becoming a Culture Action Europe member: discover all the advantages linked to the membership here. If you are interested in learning more about NRPPs and taking action for a stronger cultural presence, register for the Campaign Meeting on NRPPs on 23 September 2026 here.

Over the past year, Culture Action Europe has spent a lot of time decoding EU funding programmes that can support culture in the next seven years: AgoraEU, Horizon Europe and the European Competitiveness Fund.

But there is another, very large piece of the next EU budget that deserves considerably more attention from the cultural sector: National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs).

How large? €865 billion for 2028-2034 — almost half of the entire EU budget.

title: Hamina Tattoon käyntimäärä ylitti 100 000 - tapahtumalla on noin 8 miljoonan euron aluetaloudelliset vaikutukset
content:
Hamina Tattoo järjestettiin 27.7.-1.8.2026. Tattoon vuoden 2026 teemana oli Itämeri ja ohjelmisto piti sisällään muun muassa perinteiset Marssishow -näytökset, Tattoo-klubin, puisto- ja pihakonsertteja, Tattoo Jazz -iltoja sekä Lasten Tattoon. Tapahtuman kokonaiskäyntimäärä viikon aikana oli järjestäjän arvion mukaan 109 550.

Tapahtumasta toteutettiin laajamittainen kävijätutkimus. Tutkimuksen avulla haluttiin muun muassa päästä tarkemmin kiinni Tattoon kävijäprofiiliin, kävijöiden tyytyväisyyteen, viestinnän toimivuuteen, sekä tapahtuman aluetaloudellisiin vaikutuksiin.

Tuloksista selviää muun muassa, että Hamina Tattoon kävijät ovat erittäin sitoutuneita. Suurin osa vastaajista oli käynyt tapahtumassa aiemmin ja 31 prosenttia vastanneista oli käynyt tapahtumassa yli 10 kertaa. Toisaalta tapahtuma houkutteli hyvin myös ensikertalaisia, joita oli 18 prosenttia. content:
Vuoden kotiseututeos 2026 -finaaliin on valittu kolme teosta 43 kilpailuun ilmoitetun kirjan joukosta. title: Nu leder Tomas Höglund nämnden för Kristinestads kulturfond
content:
I september tar Svenska kulturfonden emot ansökningar om bidrag ur Kristinestads kulturfond. Tomas Höglund är ny ordförande för Svenska kulturfondens delegation och leder därmed också nämnden för Kristinestads kulturfond. 

– Via Kristinestads kulturfond kan vi erbjuda ett bra tillägg till finansieringen för många aktörer inom kultur, säger Tomas Höglund (på bilden) som från och med augusti har uppdraget som ordförande för Svenska kulturfondens delegation och Kristinestads kulturfonds nämnd.

Tomas Höglund, som har sina rötter i Jakobstad och idag jobbar som klass- och musiklärare i Esbo, är för många mera känd som en väletablerad musiker och sångare. 

– Det händer mycket inom både utbildningen och kulturen idag. Dessutom finns det inom många branscher ett stort behov av litet extra finansiering. Så jag ser fram emot att läsa alla ansökningar, det blir både givande och lärorikt, säger Tomas Höglund.

I nämnden för Kristinestads kulturfond flankeras han av Linda Sjöholm, som deltar i egenskap av släkting till donatorn Carl Sjöblom, och rektor Peter Grannas, som deltar som representant för stadens svenska fullmäktigegrupp.

title: Nytt stipendium för forskningsvistelse i Sverige
content:
Kungl. Vitterhets Historie och Antikvitets Akademien (KVHAA) och Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland (SLS) utlyser mobilitetsstipendier inom det nyetablerade Porthanprogrammet, vars syfte är att stärka forskningssamarbetet mellan Sverige och Finland inom humaniora och samhällsvetenskaper.

Programmet är uppkallat efter Henrik Gabriel Porthan, professor i vältalighet, föregångare inom
finländsk historieforskning och den första finländska ledamoten i Vitterhetsakademien (1788). I
Porthans anda främjar programmet fördjupad samverkan mellan forskare och institutioner i de två
länderna.

Vem kan ansöka?

Utlysningen riktas till disputerade forskare inom humaniora och samhällsvetenskaper, oberoende
av karriärålder, som önskar genomföra en 1–2 månader lång forskningsvistelse i grannlandet.
Vistelsen ska vara knuten till ett universitet eller en högskola, alternativt till forskning i arkiv eller
bibliotek som del av ett pågående forskningsprojekt.

Stipendiesumman är: 5 000 euro per månad (för forskare verksamma i Finland som ska vistas i
Sverige) eller 50 000 kronor per månad (för forskare verksamma i Sverige som ska vistas i Finland).

title: “My life often feels like a comedy”: Reed Still on making art, perceiving institutional systems, and residing in the Künstlerhaus Bethanien
content:
Jumping head-first into a small inflatable pool at the age of four. That takes a certain amount of trust in one’s own imagination. Besides that, it took a lot of studying afterwards. Plenty of paperwork. A lot of failing and moving around. Talking to all kinds of people. Not settling down but often settling for less. I’ve yet to undertake a medical examination to find out why exactly.

As an artist, especially for one without money, one just applies to anything that comes up. That’s most of the work before the work that the audience perceives as the artist’s work actually happens. But it’s a lot of work nonetheless. A lot of precarity. So to get access to monthly income, a studio, along with other opportunities, is an absolutely wonderful opportunity as far as opportunities in this field of unfortunately scarce opportunities go. And to be sure, there have been plenty of people around here before me at Künstlerhaus Bethanien checking in on these said opportunities, in one form or another. Marina Abramović. Susan Sontag. content:
Vuoden 2026 toinen gradustipendiaatti on Annika Haapaniemi Turun yliopistosta. Haapaniemen pääaineena on Euroopan ja maailman historia ja sivuaineenaan hänellä on Klassillinen arkeologia. Villa Lantessa Haapaniemi työstää pro gradu-tutkielmaansa, jossa hän tutkii eläinten roolia Galenoksen lääketieteessä ja erityisesti Galenoksen anatomiassa. Haapaniemi tutkii Galenoksen leikkauspöydälle joutuneiden eläinten roolia anatomisen ja lääketieteellisen tiedon tuottamisessa sekä soveltaa monilajisuuden tutkimuksen näkökulmaa tarkastellessaan näiden eläinten toimijuutta.

Roomassa ollessaan Haapaniemi aikoo hyödyntää niin Villa Lanten kuin muidenkin instituutioiden tieteellisiä kirjastoja sekä ainutlaatuista mahdollisuutta keskittyä yksinomaan tutkielman työstämiseen.

The integration of young people into the workforce can only be achieved through engagement with those who drive economic activity. This is why the IECD forges strategic partnerships with companies operating in growth sectors: agriculture, hospitality and catering, energy, industry, construction and transport. title: From Curation to Integration: What SSHOMP Can Do for Your National Research Infrastructure
content:
The SSH Open Marketplace (SSHOMP) is a discovery portal for Social Sciences and Humanities (SSH) research communities, pooling tools, services, training materials, datasets, publications, and workflows into a single searchable environment. 

But SSHOMP is not just a place to find resources: it is infrastructure you can build on. For national research initiatives, consortia, and projects, it opens up two complementary pathways that can dramatically reduce the effort required to achieve European-scale visibility — or to launch a full catalogue of digital humanities resources without building one from scratch.

The most direct way to engage with SSHOMP is to contribute your own resources. Once your tools, datasets, or services are described in the Marketplace, they become discoverable by researchers across Europe and beyond — not as isolated entries, but as nodes in a rich, interconnected network.

title: Digital Tribulations 24: Perspectives of Digital Liberation in Latin America Between Dependency, Labor, and Automation – Interview with Juan Martin Graña
content:
The introduction of Digital Tribulations, a series of intellectual interviews on the developments of digital sovereignty in Latin America, can be read here and the entire series can be found here.

I met Juan Martín Graña, a CONICET researcher, one morning in early April in Buenos Aires, at a café called Aromi, near Parque Centenario, in the Caballito neighborhood. We were put in touch by Cecilia Rikap, who recently published the book Teoría de la Dependencia Digital, so far only available in Spanish, and whose book presentation, held at the public School of Economics of the UBA, I attended in a packed room. 

Juan and I sat down at a large round table, ordered the inevitable coffee and medialunas, and began talking for about an hour about the political economy of digital dependency in Latin America. Over the course of the long conversation, Juan Martín laid out a framework that challenges mainstream narratives about automation and job loss in the Global South, arguing that the real risk is not mass unemployment but a deepening technological gap that translates into low wages and precarious work.

title: The Ancient Greek Water Clock That Kept the Most Accurate Time for 1,800 Years
content:
Today, we’re surrounded by technologies we could justifiably describe as time thieves. In ancient Greece, those who wanted to know where their time was going consulted a device they called a “water thief.” The roots of the clepsydra, or water clock, go back as far as the sixteenth century BC, with evidence of such devices found in modern-day Iraq, Iran, and Egypt, and more ambiguous evidence unearthed in places like India and China. The mechanism in the earliest examples takes not much more complex a form than a bowl out of which water slowly drips, albeit not at a regular pace. That natural impediment to hydraulic timekeeping wasn’t corrected until the third century BC, when a Greek inventor called Ctesibius set about making his own improvements.

Ctesibius’ automatic water clock used a vertical cylinder, rotating once yearly, marked with straight vertical lines representing the months of the year and curved horizontal lines representing the hours of the day. A pointer next to it indicated the current hour, its position changed by the water level of the cylinder in which it floated. That cylinder was filled through a feeding reservoir, itself constantly supplied with water.

title: Foreign-Built US Warships? It Might Work
content:
The United States lacks warships. A shipbuilding sector still suited to peacetime, a fast-multiplying Chinese navy, and allied yards offering impressive capabilities are aligning to provide new options for Washington.

The Trump administration has made revitalizing American shipbuilding a major policy priority, but this will take time. As the 2026 Maritime Action Plan stated: “The United States does not have the capacity necessary to scale up the domestic shipbuilding industry to the rate required to meet national priorities.”

What to do? In an August 13 presidential memorandum on Rebuilding the United States Navy and America’s Shipbuilding Industrial Base, the White House advocated what it called the “Finland Model” of allied shipbuilding to allow the first two ships in multi-ship buys to be constructed in select foreign shipyards in exchange for, or in response to, robust investment in America’s maritime industrial base.

title: COMMUNIA Salon: The Rodin Case
content:
On 13 October, 14:00 to 15:00 CEST, join us for a new COMMUNIA Salon exploring the French “Rodin case” and a deceptively simple question at the heart of access to cultural heritage: Should 3D scans of works in the Public Domain be freely available for reuse, including for commercial purposes?

The dispute at hand, the so-called “Rodin Case”, started in 2018, when American artist Cosmo Wenman requested access to 3D scans of several sculptures by Auguste Rodin held by the Musée Rodin. France’s Commission for Access to Administrative Documents (CADA) backed his request, but the museum refused to release the files. In 2023, the Administrative Court of Paris piled on more pressure, ordering the museum to provide access.

However, instead of putting this dispute to bed once and for all, the case then made its way to the Council of State which,  in December 2025, reversed course. Unlike previous instances, it ruled that the collections of cultural heritage institutions do not constitute administrative documents and that the Musée Rodin was therefore not required to provide access to the scans.

title: Cops Play Hide and Seek About Using Spy Tech to Avoid Scrutiny and Bad PR
content:
Law enforcement agencies across the country are increasingly relying on spying technologies—automated license plate readers (ALPR), cell-site simulators, and facial recognition, to name a few--causing an outcry in many communities where people are rightly concerned about the threat to civil rights and civil liberties these tools present.

Some authorities are responding to these concerns by trying to hide what they’re doing. Police departments are telling officers not to mention ALPRs when stopping vehicles and concealing their use of ALPRs to avoid citizens’ public records requests. Concealing the use of unpopular spying tools isn’t anything particularly new for law enforcement—cops have been doing it for years—but it’s just as wrong now as it was 20 years ago.

These practices prevent the public from knowing about and questioning how agencies are spending taxpayer dollars on spying technologies and holding them accountable. This is especially troubling when many towns are signing contracts with Flock and other ALPR vendors with little to no public oversight. The practice also violates disclosure obligations, allows cops and prosecutors to hide their tactics from judges, and cheats defendants from being able to challenge the use of evidence gathered by spy tech from being used against them.

404 Media recently revealed that in its usage policy for Flock ALPR cameras, one county in Iowa tells police to keep them a secret when detaining people: “DO NOT MENTION ALPR USAGE TO THE OCCUPANTS OF THE VEHICLE,” the policy document reads. “DO NOT MENTION ALPR USAGE IN YOUR REPORT OR COMPLAINT UNLESS ABSOLUTELY NECESSARY.” If writing a report about an incident, police are told to say they used “county resources” in making a stop instead of acknowledging use of ALPRs.

In Houston, police officers are likewise instructed to “be as vague as permissible” about why they are using Flock because the searches they run on Flock’s surveillance system could be obtained via public records requests.

There is growing public alarm about the threat to civil liberties posed by ALPR cameras and reports of police abusing the tech by using it to spy on their exes. Some cities have the cameras covered up, and others are cancelling their use of ALPR networks. Two states have recently stepped back from ALPRs. This trend is certainly not lost on law enforcement agencies. Hiding the fact that they’re using ALPRs from Flock and other vendors is one way of avoiding scrutiny and bad PR.

But law enforcement and their spy tech vendors keeping people in the dark about the surveillance technologies trained on them predates the Flock backlash by decades. For example, AT&T built a powerful phone surveillance tool for police, called Hemisphere, in the mid 2000s, and the company required agencies not to use evidence gathered by Hemisphere in court unless there was no other admissible evidence. If evidence obtained through Hemisphere was used, police were required to recreate it through a traditional subpoena, a process they called “parallel construction.” We called it “evidence laundering.”

Likewise, police and prosecutors have taken far-reaching steps to hide from the public and courts their use of cell site simulators, also known as stingrays. Police have used these devices, which trick cell phones into connecting to them instead of phone towers to try locating suspects, to obtain people’s location data without a warrant by deceptively obtaining basic pen register orders from courts. Pen register orders are for obtaining call log data and police don’t need to prove they have probable cause to get one.

In Baltimore, for example, a judge concluded that law enforcement had used a standard pen register order to intentionally hide its use of a Stingray from the court in violation of its legal disclosure obligations, leading to a landmark 2015 privacy ruling that cops need a warrant to use the device.

That didn’t stop police from continuing to try to pull the wool over the eyes of courts and defense attorneys when they used stingrays, however. Prosecutors have accepted plea deals to hide their use of cell-site simulators and have even dropped cases rather than reveal information about their use of the technology. U.S. Marshalls have driven files hundreds of miles to thwart public records requests.

Fortunately, our commitment to shining a light on the use of surveillance tech is just as strong, if not stronger, than law enforcement’s quest to hide it. We’re working with privacy advocates and community groups to bring awareness about existing and emerging spy tools that threaten civil liberties and we’re encouraging policymakers and lawmakers to do more to restrain warrantless mass surveillance and stop it before it ever takes hold.

title: New Guidance for Indigenous Collections and Data
content:
Guidance for Indigenous Collections and Indigenous Data: Recommendations from Creative Commons and Local Contexts is a new resource for cultural institution staff and cultural heritage practitioners to protect Indigenous rights within belongings and data.

The Guidance was authored by Local Contexts’ Hop Hopkins, Jane Anderson, Maui Hudson (Whakatōhea), and Corrie Roe; and Vanessa Smith, JD/MBA Candidate at UCLA. 

An approachable, practical resource, case studies within the Guidance exemplify how the Local Contexts Labels and Notices and Creative Commons licenses are complementary and can be used together to provide better protection and nuance to cultural belongings and data.

On 1 September, Creative Commons hosted a webinar with the authors of the Guidance and Anne Young, Director of Legal Affairs and Intellectual Property at the Indianapolis Museum of Art at Newfields. The recording is available on Creative Commons’ YouTube.

Creative Commons published a blog post about the Guidance and webinar with some background to the publication, insights from the webinar, and invitation to learn more.

title: Bernie Sanders to host AI briefing for US senators
content:
Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) will host a private briefing for senators next week with top artificial intelligence researchers, according to a letter to colleagues obtained by POLITICO.

The meeting, slated for 4 p.m. on Sept. 16, comes as concerns grow on both sides of the aisle about safety warnings from top AI labs and researchers about the technology’s growing capabilities.

“Congress needs SERIOUS discussions about this issue,” Sanders wrote. “That is why I will be convening a private briefing with some of the leading experts in the world to discuss this recent incident and the extraordinary dangers that AI poses for humanity.”

Geoffrey Hinton, widely known as the “godfather of AI,” is expected to brief the lawmakers alongside MIT professor and co-founder of the Future of Life Institute Max Tegmark and Ajeya Cotra, an independent investigator who helped probe OpenAI agents’ recent autonomous attack on the tech platform Hugging Face.

title: Israel/OPT: Settlement trade restrictions must be followed by further concrete measures to end Israel’s unlawful occupation and apartheid
content:
Responding to the announcement by Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Sweden and the UK that they plan to restrict trade with illegal Israeli settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territory and are considering further measures, Amnesty International’s Senior Director for Research Advocacy, Policy and Campaigns, Erika Guevara Rosas said:  

“The announcement that 12 states plan to introduce restrictions on trade with Israeli settlements, which are illegal under international humanitarian law, is a welcome, if long overdue, development that must pave the way for the adoption of further measures to bring an end to Israel’s unlawful occupation and institutionalized system of apartheid imposed against Palestinians. 

“The measures announced so far, while important, fall far short of meeting the International Court of Justice’s July 2024 instructions to states ‘not to render aid or assistance’ in maintaining Israel’s unlawful occupation of the Palestinian Territory.

title: Identities of Two More Sunni Citizens Arrested in Ahvaz Confirmed
content:
According to HRANA, two more Sunni citizens arrested in Ahvaz have been identified as Abdolmajid Sharifi, 44, and his 17-year-old son, Arkan Sharifi.

The two citizens, along with at least eight others, were arrested on Friday, September 4, 2026, after intelligence agents entered a private residence in the Kuy-e Mashali neighborhood of Ahvaz.

According to information received by HRANA, the citizens had gathered at a friend’s home for a meeting when intelligence agents surrounded the residence, entered the home, and arrested at least 10 of those present.

Reports received by HRANA also indicate that some of the citizens were beaten during their arrests and subsequently transferred to an undisclosed location.

HRANA had previously identified three other detainees: Razi Heydari, 50; Hossein Heydari, 29; and Abdolhadi Asakereh, 30. With the identification of Abdolmajid Sharifi and Arkan Sharifi, the identities of five of the detainees have now been confirmed.

These citizens are residents of the Kuy-e Mashali and Akhar-e Asfalt neighborhoods of Ahvaz.

title: Indonesian Military Court Reduces Acid Attack Sentences
content:
A military court in Jakarta reduced the prison sentences and overturned the dishonorable discharge of two of the four military personnel convicted for the March 2026 acid attack against human rights activist Andrie Yunus. 

The appellate decision, dated August 20, reduced the sentences of 2nd Sgt. Edi Sudarko and 1st Lt. Budhi Hariyanto Widhi Cahyono of the Indonesian military’s Strategic Intelligence Agency (BAIS) by six months, bringing both sentences to less than three years. The appeals court upheld the shorter sentences of the other two defendants, Capt. Nandala Dwi Prasetya and 1st Lt. Sami Lakka.

On March 12, Yunus, 27, the deputy coordinator of KontraS, the nongovernmental Commission for the Disappeared and Victims of Violence, had just finished recording a podcast interview at the Indonesian Legal Aid Foundation when he was attacked with acid. He received 24 percent burns to his face, chest, and hands, and may have lost sight in his right eye. On June 10, a military court found all four soldiers guilty of planning and carrying out the attack.

title: Labor Day and the Democracy We Deny Workers
content:
By Sam Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 9 September 2026 (IDN) — Every Labor Day, Americans perform a familiar ritual. Politicians praise the dignity of work. Corporations thank their employees. Newspapers recall the struggles of the labor movement. Families mark the unofficial end of summer with barbecues and a final long weekend. Then Tuesday arrives, and tens of millions of Americans return to workplaces over which they exercise remarkably little control.

They may elect a president, a governor, a mayor, a senator. They may vote on referenda and school boards. They are told from childhood that legitimate authority derives from the consent of the governed. But for eight or ten hours a day, five days a week, most enter institutions in which this principle largely disappears.

Their schedules may be altered. Their workloads may increase. Their jobs may be eliminated. Their workplaces may be reorganized, monitored, automated, relocated or closed. Decisions affecting their income, security, health and future are routinely made by people they did not elect and frequently have no meaningful power to challenge.

title: Volvo, Candy, Pirelli: China is buying up Europe. Conspiracy or capitalism?
content:
Concerns over China’s growing economic power are particularly acute in Brussels and Washington. Yet step outside the corridors of government and onto the streets of European capitals, and it quickly becomes clear that this alarm may have come at least a decade too late. BYD showrooms are now part of the urban landscape in Warsaw, while the Chinese carmaker openly sponsors local cultural events, including open-air cinemas.

Temu and Shein parcels have become a familiar sight in European homes, while Huawei technology has long played a significant role in the continent’s telecommunications infrastructure. China has proved remarkably effective at identifying gaps in Western markets and exploiting vulnerabilities that Europe itself helped create. Crucially, it has done so while operating under an economic model fundamentally different from the traditional Western version of capitalism.

title: Rumours of voter fraud spread after voting problems in Sweden
content:
“Voter fraud everywhere,” a person wrote on X about advance votes that were incorrectly registered. But the Swedish Election Authority rejects the claim, NORDIS partner Källkritikbyrån reports.

Last Friday the Swedish Election Authority reported a technical error that was then feared to affect approximately 4,000 advance votes. Over the weekend, the error concerning advance votes was analysed, and it was found that at most 500 advance votes are affected.

The figure may decrease further, the Swedish Election Authority writes on its website, and regrets that it will probably not be possible to determine who cast these votes.

– The error occurred because election officials began accepting a new vote before they had completed the voting process for the previous voter. As a result, the votes were registered incorrectly, Jenny Stad, press officer at the Swedish Election Authority, told Källkritikbyrån.

Post on X on 4 September.

title: Automattic CEO Matt Mullenweg Put on 'Leave of Absence'
content:
On a company-wide Slack this morning, Automattic CEO Matt Mullenweg announced he has been put on a paid leave of absence.

“And the biggest news: I won't be able to make the ELT tomorrow,” Matt wrote in an Announcement Slack. He continued, writing that Mark Davies, current Automattic Chief Financial Officer, has “conspired” with Automattic Board of Directors members Ann Dunwoody, Toni Schneider, and Sue Decker “behind my back and they voted to put me on a paid leave of absence. I voted against that.” 

He wrote that Davies was voted to be the new interim CEO. “I received the resolution 50 minutes before the meeting start, and requested repeatedly for time to have it reviewed by independent legal counsel, even a few hours, which was denied,” Mullenweg wrote.

Mullenweg is the founder of Automattic, the company that owns WordPress, Tumblr, Pocket Casts, and a host of other popular internet brands and pieces of software. Mullenweg has faced several controversies over his management of the company in recent years.

In the same Slack channel, Davies wrote that Mullenweg would remain a board member and “he will have a voice in setting direction and making decisions.”

title: When it's OK for a newsroom to fail in public — plus our sold-out AI x Investigative Forum
content:
Journalism gets one shot to be right. Product work gets better every time something breaks. Frank Bi, who joins us as our AI Strategy & Product Advisor, launched the Minnesota Star Tribune's first two audience-facing AI products, and he's written up how to hold both truths at once: put experiments behind a clearly labeled sandbox, give each one an end date before it launches, and let the readers who opt in show you what actually works. Now that anyone with a laptop can ship code, the newsrooms that learn fastest will be the ones willing to be wrong at the start to be right at the end.

A hand-drawn guide to AI in investigations from The Times. Three newsrooms on how they used AI to comb the Epstein Files. Reuters reporting from document dumps too big to read, CNN vibe coding a flight-tracking pipeline and CUNY automating the grind of backgrounding a subject. That's the program for our forum a The New York Times on Friday, Sept. 25. It's sold out, but the full program is online now and we'll publish takeaways afterward for everyone who couldn't attend.

title: Turkey Detains 24 in Belgium-Linked Drug Trafficking Probe
content:
Turkish authorities have detained 24 people and seized assets worth approximately $20.6 million in an operation targeting an international drug trafficking network allegedly directed from Belgium, the Justice Ministry said.

The Izmir Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office issued detention warrants for 38 suspects. Eleven of the individuals are believed to be abroad, one is already incarcerated, and police are searching for two remaining suspects.

Authorities seized 87 properties, 18 vehicles, four private boats, stakes in 14 companies, and bank accounts suspected of representing crime proceeds.

Prosecutors did not disclose the identities of the suspects, the specific types or quantities of drugs involved, or other countries where the syndicate operated. Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said investigators are targeting both the syndicate's members and the corporate vehicles used to launder illicit funds.

title: Ectopic Pregnancy Deaths Have Nearly Doubled. It’s Worse in States With Abortion Bans.
content:
The number of women who died after an ectopic pregnancy has spiked in recent years, a ProPublica analysis found. The mounting deaths in Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data have drawn little scrutiny or response.

Such deaths typically occur in the first trimester, after a pregnancy fails to properly implant in the uterus and begins to develop elsewhere, most commonly inside a fallopian tube. The embryo grows until it causes the organ to rupture, triggering catastrophic bleeding. 

With prompt and appropriate medical care, maternal health experts say, women should not die. Yet ProPublica’s analysis found a stark and baffling increase: Almost 200 women with the condition died from 2020 to 2025, compared with about 100 in the previous six years.

“A death related to ectopic pregnancy should really be a never event,” said Dr. Alice Abernathy, an OB-GYN in Philadelphia.

While chaos and access issues at hospitals during the COVID-19 pandemic likely contributed to at least some of the deaths, the surge has persisted, raising serious questions about the role of the most significant disruption to maternal healthcare in the years since: state restrictions on abortion.

title: Minä töissä: näytelmäkirjailija Pipsa Enqvist
content:
Pipsa Enqvist

Olen Pipsa Enqvist näytelmäkirjailija, ohjaaja ja dramaturgi. Kirjoittamani näytelmä Väliintulo sai juuri Kajaanin kaupunginteatterissa ensi-iltansa. Vuonna 2024 sain Kouran pääpalkinnon yhdessä Amira Rchidin ja Amaal Alin kanssa Ylelle käsikirjoittamastamme draamasarjasta What would Samira do? Toimin sarjassa myös ohjaajana. 

Mitä on työpöydälläsi tällä hetkellä tai mikä teos saa ensi-iltansa piakkoin?

Kirjoitan paraikaa näytelmää Siis kaunis koululinna loista, joka käsittelee suomalaisen peruskoulutuksen historiaa,  koulutuksellista ihmiskuvaa, oppivelvollisuuspolitiikkaa ja sitä, millaisiksi ihmisiksi koulussa eri aikoina on haluttu kasvattaa. Näytelmässä kysytään, mikä on oppimisen arvoista ja miksi. Teos toteutetaan Kolmas tila -kollektiivin kanssa Turussa. Ensi-ilta on lokakuun lopulla.

Kerro viimeisimmästä teoksestasi.

title: Why France’s illustrious history of cheesemaking is full of holes
content:
The famous words of General de Gaulle – “How can you govern a country where there are 246 varieties of cheese?” – show just how closely regional identities are linked to a country’s cheesemaking heritage that seems to be rooted in ancient history. And yet this is both true and false, as this tradition that the French are so proud of only dates back five or six generations.

Exploring the subject of cheese produced by the distant and not so distant ancestors of modern-day France, proves difficult for various reasons. On the one hand, cheeses discovered in an archaeological context are rare: those from the Bronze Age are the exception that proves the rule and were only able to have been preserved thanks to specific climatic conditions. The cheeses of the past were, in actual fact, different from the cheeses we know today and they belonged to societies with gastronomic values and tastes distinct from our own.

title: Maailmassa on nyt neljä virallista terapiametsää
content:
Metsässä oleskelulla on tunnetusti myönteisiä vaikutuksia. Metsälenkki on monelle paras tapa rentoutua vaikkapa työkiireiden jälkeen, ja myös tutkimusten mukaan metsässä oleskelu voi auttaa sairauksien ehkäisemisessä ja stressin vähentämisessä – mahdollisesti jopa verenpaineen alentamisessa.

Nyt huomiota saa myös metsien terapiapotentiaali. Maailmassa on neljä metsää, jotka ovat saaneet saksalaiselta Healing Forest International Certification Officelta sertifikaatin siitä, että ne voivat toimia terapeuttisina metsinä.

Uusin on heinäkuussa sertifioitu Bussacon metsä Portugalissa, muut sijaitsevat Itävallassa ja Saksassa, kertoo Euronews.

Terapeuttinen metsä on lähes luonnontilainen metsäalue, jossa tarjotaan koulutettujen metsä­terapeuttien palveluita. Metsien pitää tarjota myös näkö- ja melusuojaa, suojaa tuulelta, niissä pitää olla eritasoisia polkuja sekä alueita, joilla voi harjoittaa terapiaa ja rentoutua.

Suomalaisia metsiä ei toistaiseksi ole terapiametsälistalla. Metsäterapiaa kuitenkin toteutetaan, ja maa- ja metsätalousministeriön rahoituksella on kehitetty myös Terveysmetsä-hyvinvointimenetelmä.

Terveysmetsiä löytyy muun muassa Hyvinkäältä, Lahdesta, Kajaanista ja Kouvolasta.

title: A New Kind Of Creative Poverty
content:
Editor’s Note: Noema is transparent about AI use in its pieces. We publish original human-generated ideas but allow authorized, disclosed use of AI in certain cases. Please see details at the end of this piece.

During a dark stretch of Covid, I dove into Joan Didion’s “The Year of Magical Thinking,” her book about processing her husband’s death. Didion wrote that she could not give away his shoes. She had managed the suits, the shirts, the jackets. But when she got to the shoes, she paused: “I stood there for a moment, then realized why: he would need shoes if he was to return.”

I was living in solitude in an apartment recently emptied by a long-term relationship. When the rental lease lapsed, I renewed it and renewed it again, keeping the furniture exactly as it had been, the lamp at the same angle. What Didion was dealing with was, in Orwell’s words,  “the recognizable experiences of human beings.” Through her writing, I felt relief wash over me as I suddenly saw my own stalled life right under my nose.

title: Democracy meatballs: why IKEA is the place for Swedes abroad to vote
content:
For most Australians and New Zealanders, IKEA is where you go for a BILLY bookcase, Swedish meatballs and a trolley full of purchases you never intended to make.

But in the lead-up to Sweden’s election on September 13 2026, some IKEA stores have taken on an unexpected new role. In Brisbane, Adelaide and Auckland – alongside Hyderabad, India – Swedish citizens were invited to cast their votes inside the furniture giant’s blue-and-yellow stores.

The Swedish Election Authority expanded the number of overseas voting locations for the 2026 election from around 266 locations in 2022 to approximately 290 worldwide.

In some places, this meant temporary voting locations at IKEA stores.

At one level, using IKEA makes perfect practical sense. The stores are easy to find, centrally located and familiar to many Swedish expatriates. But convenience is not the only factor.

IKEA is closely associated with “home” for many Swedes.

The first IKEA store opened in Älmhult, Sweden, in 1958. The first IKEA outside of Sweden opened in Norway in 1963, and the company reached Australia by 1975. There are now over 500 stores in more than 60 countries.

title: IS: Antti Rinne palaa kansanedustajaksi
content:
SDP:n entinen puheenjohtaja Antti Rinne ottaa varasijalta saamansa kansanedustajuuden vastaan ja palaa eduskuntaan, kertoo Ilta-Sanomat.

Rinne (s. 1962) tulee demariryhmästä elinkeinoelämän johtotehtäviin siirtyneen Miapetra Kumpula-Natrin tilalle.

Rinne erosi hallituskumppanien luottamuskriisin takia pääministeriydestä vuonna 2019, ja tilalle tuli puolueen varapuheenjohtaja Sanna Marin. Tämä myös valittiin demarien puheenjohtajaksi syksyllä 2020. Kevään 2023 vaaleissa Rinne jäi varasijalle.

Viime syksystä asti Rinne on työskennellyt saamelaisten sovintokomission suosituksia arvioivan parlamentaarisen työryhmän pääsihteerinä.

Ilta-Sanomien haastattelussa Rinne ei vielä kerro, kiinnostaako häntä osallistua ensi kevään eduskuntavaaleihin.

title: Väitös: Eurooppalainen teknojohtaja perustaa demokratialle, ei Piilaakson visiolle
content:
Eurooppalaiset teknologia- ja alusta-alan johtajat pitävät edelleen kiinni eurooppalaisesta yhteiskuntamallista, summaa tuore tutkimus. Johtajat arvostavat Yhdysvaltojen innovaatiokykyä mutta eivät jaa Piilaakson libertaaria aatetta.

Digitaalisten alustojen valtakausi on muuttanut yhteiskuntaa yhtä perusteellisesti kuin teollistuminen aikanaan, todetaan Helsingin yliopiston tiedotteessa. Vaikka amerikkalaiset suuryritykset hallitsevat globaalia alustainfrastruktuuria, eurooppalaisilla johtajilla on silti merkittävä rooli alakohtaisten alustojen rakentamisessa Euroopassa.

Elina Kiiski-Katajan väitöstutkimuksen mukaan Piilaakson visiota on ohjannut libertaarismi, kylmän sodan innovaatiokulttuuri ja 1960-luvun vastakulttuuri. Visio korostaa individualismia ja näkee teknologian välineenä irtautua yhteiskunnan rakenteista.

Euroopan unioni on rakentanut digitaalisen sääntelynsä toisenlaiselle pohjalle: demokratialle, perusoikeuksille ja sosiaaliselle markkinataloudelle. Väitöskirja kutsuu tätä lähtökohtaa eurooppalaiseksi unelmaksi.

Kiiski-Kataja haastatteli väitöskirjaansa 20 teknologia-alan johtajaa ja vaikuttajaa eri puolilta Eurooppaa, sekä suurista että pienistä yrityksistä.

title: Drought development characteristics modulate global dry–wet abrupt alternation through distinct land–atmosphere feedbacks
content: This study shows that antecedent drought development is linked to distinct, region-dependent pathways from drought to extreme precipitation, providing a basis for anticipating compound hydrological extremes. Rapid transitions from drought to extreme precipitation can trigger cascading impacts, but the influence of antecedent drought development on subsequent precipitation remains unclear. Dry–wet abrupt alternation events were identified using a global event-scale framework and separated into successive dry and wet phases.

content:
Keskiviikko 11.11.2026 klo 9.00 – 16.00
Tieteiden talo, Kirkkokatu 6, Helsinki

Tämän tapahtuman teema on suomalaisten hyvinvointi 15-20 vuotta nykyhetkestä eteenpäin. Pohdimme yhdessä eri alojen asiantuntijoiden kanssa miten tulevaisuudessa näkyvät trendit, mahdollisuudet ja uhat vaikuttavat suomalaisiin arvoihin ja rakenteisiin. Tapahtuma on tarkoitettu kaikille tulevaisuudesta innostuneille, tulevaisuuteen kriittisesti suhtautuville, tulevaisuuksia tutkiville ja tulevaisuutta tekeville.

Tapahtumassa kahdeksan eri näkökulmia edustavaa asiantuntijaa esittää teesinsä tulevaisuudesta liittyen seuraavanlaisiin kysymyksiin: 

  • mitä nykyisissä arvoissamme ja rakenteissamme kannattaa säilyttää,
  • mitä pitäisi muuttaa,
  • millaista hyvinvointia haluamme rakentaa 2040-luvulle ja
  • miten meidän kannattaa vaikuttaa toimintaympäristöömme.

title: Provinssin ja Rytmikorjaamon yhteinen suojelumetsä löytyi Peräseinäjoelta
content:
Provinssin ja Rytmikorjaamon yleisön tuella kerätyt varat ovat johtaneet uuden suojelumetsän hankintaan Etelä-Pohjanmaalla. Peräseinäjoelta löytynyt Kortesharjun metsäalue on nyt ostettu pysyvään suojeluun Luonnonperintösäätiölle.

Provinssimetsä- ja Rytmikorjaamon metsä -kampanjat käynnistettiin vuonna 2023. Molempien hankkeiden tavoitteena oli kerätä varoja suojelumetsän perustamiseen Etelä-Pohjanmaalle. Kun Peräseinäjoelta löytyi luonnonarvoiltaan sopiva kohde, kampanjoiden varat yhdistettiin yhteisen suojelumetsän hankkimiseksi.

”Olemme iloisia siitä, että pitkäjänteinen työ tuotti tulosta ja yhteinen metsä löytyi juuri Etelä-Pohjanmaalta. Tämä on hieno osoitus siitä, mitä kulttuuritoimijat ja luonnonystävät voivat yhdessä saada aikaan”, sanoo Luonnonperintösäätiön suojelupäällikkö Vilma Kaukoranta.

title: They work for you (and we do too)
content:
We run TheyWorkForYou to make UK politics more accessible and accountable.

Here’s what we’ve been doing recently to make that happen.

Our alerts service will send you an email whenever your chosen keyword or phrase is mentioned in Parliament; or you can follow any MP or other representative to receive an email when they speak or vote.

So far in 2026, we’ve sent 2.2 million email alerts and our users have created almost 2,000 new keyword alerts through our new and improved alerts management system.

This service helps people understand what their representatives (across all of the UK’s Parliaments) are saying and doing, and also provides an essential service in providing free parliamentary monitoring to civic groups and organisations who can now have as much access to this intel as those with big pockets.

This doesn’t happen by itself: every day our team pulls together the transcripts from the UK’s Parliaments, fixing formatting issues and broken files to get these loaded into the site and our alerts.

If you don’t have alerts set up, what are you waiting for? You can do it now at TheyWorkForYou.com.

title: Dagbani Wikimedians Take Wikipedia Awareness to Radio, Promote Language Diversity Conference 2026
content:
The Dagbani Wikimedians User Group (DWUG) has stepped up its public awareness efforts to help more people understand Wikipedia, Wikimedia projects, and the role they can play in preserving and promoting Dagbani and other African languages online.

As part of this effort, members of the user group participated in radio discussions on Zaa Radio 99.3 FM on 22 August 2026 and Dagbon FM 102.5 on 5 September 2026.

Representing the Dagbani Wikimedians User Group during the radio engagements were Abdul-Rafiu Fuseini (Alhaji Darajaati), Hamidu Rukaya (Ruky Wunpini), Fuseini Mugisu Suhuyini (Sir Amugi), and Musah Fuseini (Musahfm). 

The radio engagements provided an opportunity to speak directly to listeners about the work of Wikimedians, the importance of contributing knowledge to Wikimedia projects, and the growing presence of Dagbani in the digital space.

One of the main areas discussed during the interviews was the difference between Wikipedia, Wikimedia, and Wikimedians.

title: Streaming from the cloud was meant to change games forever – what happened?
content:
Once hailed as the future, even the likes of Google, Sony and Microsoft have struggled to make streaming games fun, fast or affordable

• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

In August 2009, at the very first Gamescom expo, I sat in a small meeting room in Germany and played Mario Kart and World of Warcraft on a laptop, via technology that was then completely new: cloud gaming. It was a demonstration for a yet-to-be-launched service called Gaikai that promised to let you play any game in a browser window, without a console. (Here is an ancient video of that demonstration, featuring a very young Keza.) With a single click I could launch into any game, hosted on servers hundreds of miles away. It really did look like the future.

title: Kasvipohjaiset maidon ja lihan vaihtoehdot pääosin turvallisia, mutta eivät täysin riskittömiä
content:
Kasvipohjaiset maidon ja lihan vaihtoehdot tarjoavat kuluttajille ravitsemus- ja ympäristöhyötyjä, mutta niiden turvallisuudessa on eläinperäisistä elintarvikkeista poikkeavia erityispiirteitä. Ruokaviraston ja VTT:n katsausartikkelin mukaan näiden tuotteiden kohdalla on syytä kiinnittää huomiota etenkin homemyrkkyihin, eräisiin metalleihin sekä itiöitä muodostaviin bakteereihin.

Food Science & Nutrition -lehdessä julkaistu katsausartikkeli kokoaa yhteen tutkimustietoa kasvipohjaisten maitovalmisteiden ja lihan vaihtoehtojen kemiallisista ja mikrobiologisista vaaroista sekä ravitsemuksellisista ominaisuuksista. Katsausartikkeli perustuu kansainvälisiin tutkimuksiin, ja suomalaisista maitotuotteiden kasviperäisistä vaihtoehdoista julkaistaan tarkempaa tietoa 17.9. järjestettävässä VEGETURVA-hankkeen loppuseminaarissa.

– Kasvipohjaisten tuotteiden riskiprofiili on erilainen kuin maidolla ja lihalla. Niissä esiintyy joitakin sellaisia kemiallisia vaaroja, joita eläinperäisissä tuotteissa tavataan harvoin, mutta samalla niissä on vähemmän esimerkiksi eläinperäisiin raaka-aineisiin liittyviä taudinaiheuttajia, sanoo tutkimusprofessori Johanna Suomi Ruokavirastosta.

title: Symposium: Remembering the distant past
content:
Symposium “Remembering the distant past: cultural memory in Finland from Hammurabi to Hilma Granqvist”

When and where: 23rd of October 2026, 10 am - 5.15pm, University of Helsinki Main building (Fabianinkatu 33) room F3005

Research on cultural memory often focuses on how people of the past maintained the memory of their own past. In this symposium we focus instead on how the past is remembered in the 19th and 20th century. We focus both on the mnemonic veil of the distant past and its historical characters in publicity but also on how researchers and artists participated in remembering the past. The presentations emphasise cultural memory in the Finnish context.

The symposium is organized by ANEE+ Interdisciplinary Research Network at the University of Helsinki and the discipline of Cultural History at the University of Turku.

The event is free, but please register by 16th of October for in-person participation. The event will be live streamed.

9.45-10.00 Coffee service

10.00-10.15 Opening remarks from the organizers

title: Commission champions the next generation of European Capitals of Culture
content:
On 10 September 2026, the European Commission adopted its proposal for the new legal framework of the European Capitals of Culture action from 2034 to 2047. It will be discussed with both the European Parliament and the Council.

The European Capitals of Culture ’s current legal framework will come to an end in 2033. EU institutions thus need to determine how the action will be set up as of 2034 and ensure the initiative remains relevant, inclusive and impactful until 2047.

Based on thorough consultation and evaluation, the European Commission submitted a proposal to ensure that:

  • the action remains accessible and in line with EU priorities and current global challenges
  • the action reinforces its EU dimension
  • the right tools are provided to follow and react to the cities’ progress in implementing their programme and to plan for their legacy
  • the action remains visible by enhancing communication tools and activities

    • The proposal wants to bring more people in, make the process simpler and ensure the longer-term legacy of European Capitals of Culture.

title: First ECHOES training course launched on DARIAH-CAMPUS
content:
ECHOES has launched its first training course! Introduction to European Collaborative Cloud for Cultural Heritage aims to build learners’ foundational understanding of the key concepts and technologies necessary to engage with the Cultural Heritage Cloud. The course, available on DARIAH Campus, consists of  five units which provide the background to the development of the ECCCH, the key concepts, how collaboration works in the ECCCH, Open Science and FAIR principles and concludes with a set of illustrative scenarios.

An extract from Unit 2: Key Concepts and Foundations

In addition, ECHOES has also developed the OntoMatchGame to facilitate learning about ontological models. This educational application is in the form of a card game, providing a step-by-step guide to understanding how the ontology works and how mapping is used to associate data with ontology entities.

The training course and OntoMatchGame can both be accessed through the Capacity Building page where further information is also available.

title: Historian Timothy Snyder Teaches a Free Course on Hitler, Stalin & How “It” Can Happen Here
content:
When the historian Timothy Snyder left Yale for the University of Toronto in 2024, he took with him the practice of occasionally putting his course lectures online, making them available to anyone who cares to learn from them. Above, you can watch ten lectures from his recent course Hitler and Stalin Today. In this course:

Snyder examines the Nazi and Soviet responses to the new globalized world they shared. The course begins with the colonial background that made totalitarianism possible, and which remains an essential element of our politics now. Their ideologies are described as worldviews and as practical politics, with an emphasis on the reasons for their appeal. Attention to their policies of mass killing, essential events of twentieth-century history, instruct us about how “it” can happen here. The study of dissident thought helps us to see connections between historical predicaments and our own, and instructs us about possible reactions as individuals and as citizens. The course asks what we have learned from the twentieth century and what lessons we should carry forward.

title: Ukraine Rethinks Mine Clearance for a New Age
content:
The technology of war is evolving faster than the systems it is designed to counter. Artificial intelligence, drones, sensors, and other technologies are transforming how weapons are developed, deployed, and concealed.

The clean-up technology for mines and other explosive ordnance is not immune to these changes. Much of what organizations have learned over the decades has been made obsolete by new technologies. In Ukraine and elsewhere, a new approach is needed.

The scale of contamination is now just part of the challenge: the variety, sophistication, and concealability of explosive threats make them increasingly difficult to detect, classify, and safely neutralize.

The success or failure of Ukraine’s mine clearance will directly affect how quickly contaminated land can be returned to productive use and how successfully the country can recover, and will offer lessons for the rest of the world.

The mine problem is often framed in terms of scale: How much land is contaminated? How many munitions remain? And how much time and money will clearance require? As critical as these questions are, there is a more fundamental problem: the evolving nature of the threat.

title: Digital Sovereignty: What It Is, What It Could Be
content:
The term “digital sovereignty” has become ubiquitous. European officials invoke it in debates about cloud infrastructure, AI, semiconductors, and platform regulation. Governments throughout the global majority use it to argue for greater control over data and communications infrastructure and boost their economies. Companies market “sovereign cloud” products designed to reassure their customers that their information stays under local jurisdiction. But digital sovereignty could be something more: an opportunity for users around the world to build more resilient, open  systems and the skills and infrastructure to maintain them.

There is no singular definition of digital sovereignty, nor is there a single coherent position in the digital rights space. Despite its growing popularity, the term remains frustratingly vague. Policymakers, regulators, civil society groups, and others can mean very different things when they use the term. But to start simply with a broad definition, we can say that it means having the capacity to control one’s digital destiny—though the implications of that will obviously differ considerably whether you’re talking about an individual or a country.

title: US Democrats prepare to put AI under a new microscope
content:
House Democrats are laying the groundwork for a select committee on artificial intelligence should they retake control of the House in November, 11 people familiar with the planning told POLITICO.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has been briefed on the effort and expressed openness to the idea, four of those people said. All 11 people were granted anonymity to discuss details of private deliberations.

The discussions offer an early glimpse of how Democrats could use their new gavels and expanded oversight powers to scrutinize the tech industry.

House select committees are usually created by a full House vote and last only for the two years of the Congress that created them. Gaining buy-in from members who sit on committees that currently oversee AI policy may prove difficult.

The Energy and Commerce; Judiciary; and Science, Space and Technology committees all oversee slices of the AI policy portfolio. Its chairs and members will likely be reluctant to give up any jurisdiction of the issue, especially at a pivotal stage in shaping the rules governing the technology, two of the people said.

title: Durban Conference 25 years on. Mandi Mudarikwa: “It’s up to us all to build the kind of world we want to live in”
content:
The third UN Conference Against Racism, Racial Discrimination, Xenophobia and Related Intolerance in 2001 was a watershed moment for millions across the world. Seven thousand people representing governments and civil society from 170 countries gathered in Durban, South Africa. Led by countries in the Global South, the Durban Conference challenged the idea that human rights is a Western concept, recognized the historical roots of contemporary forms of racism and called on States to repair the lasting consequences of colonialism and slavery. While the US and Israel withdrew from the Conference, the Durban Declaration and Programme of Action were adopted, both of which became foundational documents for the global fight against racism. But with racism still very much alive, we spoke with activists about their struggles and hopes. 

My name is Mandi Mudarikwa and I’m a human rights strategic litigator at Amnesty International. My legal career has been about using law and the courts as instruments of justice, accountability, and the advancement and enjoyment of human rights.

title: Freedom House Adopts Case of Imprisoned Belarusian Civil Society Expert Tatiana Kouzina
content:
Washington, DC—Freedom House announced today that the Fred Hiatt Program to Free Political Prisoners has adopted the case of imprisoned Belarusian civil society expert Tatiana Kouzina.

“Freedom House is proud to stand with Tatiana Kouzina and fight for her release. As we have documented, Belarus’s political regime is one of the most repressive in the world, featuring rigged elections, severe restrictions on journalists and civil society, and a judiciary subservient to the country’s authoritarian President Alyaksandr Lukashenka, who has been in power since 1994,” said Jamie Fly, CEO of Freedom House “It is tragic but not surprising that the Lukashenka regime would imprison experts like Tatiana, who could otherwise serve as an independent source of information and a credible voice of dissent. We call for Tatiana to be immediately and unconditionally released.”

title: January 2026 Protests: Report on the Latest Condition of Mojtaba Azhadi in Mashhad’s Vakilabad Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Mojtaba Azhadi remains incarcerated in Mashhad’s Vakilabad Prison.

According to information received by HRANA, Azhadi remains in legal limbo at Vakilabad Prison. Despite 238 days having passed since his arrest, no trial has yet been held, nor has he been granted the possibility of temporary release on bail.

An informed source close to his family confirmed the situation to HRANA, stating: “During the protests in January of last year, he was struck by pellet gunfire in the face and neck. Despite undergoing surgery, several pellets remain lodged in his forehead, with another pellet behind his eye. Azhadi requires medical treatment and surgery to remove the pellets from his face, but due to obstruction by the relevant authorities, he has been denied transfer to a hospital outside the prison.”

title: China Wants Citizens to Report ‘Illegal’ Religious Practice
content:
Chinese lawyer Ruth Wang fled to Taiwan on September 2 after authorities threatened to shut down her law firm. Her offense? Representing members of China’s Zion Church, a prominent underground Protestant congregation.

While founding pastor Ezra Jin was freed from custody in July following high-level US intervention, eight other church members have remained wrongfully detained since their October 2025 arrests.

Chinese leader Xi Jinping launched his “Sinicization of religion” policy in 2016, which included government regulations tightening controls over religious life. Beijing is not only punishing people for independent religious practice but also those defending their rights.

Recently, authorities have continued to tighten surveillance over religious activities. In the first half of 2026 alone, more than a dozen cities across the country introduced measures encouraging or rewarding people to report religious activities the government labels “illegal.” The reporting rules are sweeping.

title: 25 Years of War Was the Wrong Response to 9/11
content:
By Medea Benjamin and Nicolas J. S.Davies*

NEW YORK | 9 September 2026 (IDN) — The lesson of 9/11 should be that war is not the answer to any of the problems facing the United States. After inflicting violence and chaos on country after country for twenty-five years in a “global war on terror” that has evolved into a Zionist genocide and a revived Cold War against Russia and China, the widespread public opposition to Trump’s war on Iran suggests that most Americans have finally learned that lesson.

Unfortunately, powerful sections of our corrupt business and political elites have not.

Most Americans old enough to remember September 11, 2001, can still recall the horrifying images played endlessly on our TV screens as the scale of the mass murder became clear. But we also remember something else: the sinking feeling that the hopes and dreams of billions of people, in the US and around the world, would be pushed to the back-burner for the foreseeable future, as our leaders and corporate media all too predictably embraced a new agenda of revenge, fear-mongering, jingoism and military violence.

title: I Wrote About His Wrongful Conviction. He Got Only 13 Years of Freedom Before Cancer Took His Life.
content:
I’d like to tell you about Fred Steese, who died in August of cancer at 62. When I first met Fred, he was living hand to mouth in a seedy motel on the outskirts of Las Vegas. He had been released from prison a couple of years earlier and struggled to find stable housing and a job, because — on paper, at least — Fred appeared to be a convicted murderer. 

In 1995, Fred was wrongfully convicted of the murder of Gerard Soules — a former trapeze artist who had a dancing poodle show at a Las Vegas casino — even though prosecutors had evidence that he was hundreds of miles away at the time. He then spent 21 years in prison before a judge declared him innocent. 

I wrote about Fred in a 2017 ProPublica and Vanity Fair story. It was part of a series that investigated how an obscure type of plea deal was shaping innocence cases and giving cover to district attorney offices that didn’t want to admit wrongdoing — or examine prosecutorial misconduct.

title: Arzu Hatakoy
content: Arzu Hatakoy was appointed as Head of Office, Syria, in August 2026. She brings 20 years of experience in humanitarian-development-peace coordination in complex and high-risk environments. Prior to this role, Arzu served as Principal Coordination Officer with the UN Assistance Mission to Afghanistan (UNAMA) and head of RCO in Kabul, where she provided strategic leadership in advancing UN system-wide coordination and strengthening engagement with de facto authorities and international stakeholders. She also previously led the UNAMA Office in Herat. Arzu started her UN career with OCHA in 2007, where she held several positions, including as Deputy Head of Office in Gaziantep, Türkiye. She has worked on large-scale humanitarian responses, particularly in the Middle East and Africa. Arzu also served with the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process in Jerusalem. In addition to her UN experience, she led the GIZ Syria Peace Initiative project based in Beirut. Arzu holds a Doctorate in Political Science from the Free University of Berlin, a Master in Public Administration from Harvard Kennedy School and a Master in International Relations from Sciences Po Paris. A German national, Arzu is fluent in English and French, a native speaker of German and Turkish, and has beginners’ level of Persian and Arabic.
